title: Venezuelan Arepas with Butter and Grated White Cheese
summary: Masarepa dough is shaped into discs, seared in a heavy pan until crusted, baked until they sound hollow, then split and filled with butter and grated white cheese.
equipment: large cast-iron or heavy frying pan

ingredients.item: precooked white corn flour (masarepa, such as P.A.N.)
fine sea salt or table salt
queso fresco or mild white cheese, grated

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Whisk the salt into the warm water, then add the corn flour gradually, mixing with your hand until no dry lumps remain. Cover with the towel and rest for 5 minutes. It should feel like soft play dough; add 1-2 tbsp water if it cracks.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Divide into 8 balls (about 110 g each). With damp hands, flatten each into a 10 cm disc about 1.5 cm thick, smoothing any cracked edges.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Heat the oil in the pan over medium heat and cook the arepas in batches for 5-6 minutes per side until a pale golden crust forms.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Move them to the tray and bake for 10-15 minutes until slightly puffed and hollow-sounding when tapped.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Cool for 2 minutes on the rack, then split each almost all the way through, spread with butter and stuff with cheese. Serve hot.

tips: Use precooked corn flour (masarepa); masa harina or cornmeal will not hold together.
Smooth cracks at the edge before cooking, or the arepas split in the pan.
Try other fillings: black beans, shredded chicken or avocado.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Cooled unfilled arepas keep in the fridge for 3 days or the freezer for a month; reheat in a 180 °C oven for 10 minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
